II
                                  FOREWORD



     Information for this publication is based on a survey of excepted positions
in the Federal Government as of September 3, 1976.

    Since the first publication of Policy and Supporting Positions in 1960, an
impression has developed that it is a list of "political jobs," or a "Plum Book"
connoting its use by a new Administration to make appointments in the Exec-
utive Branch. To an extent, this is true; individuals who serve at the pleasure
of the President or as confidential assistants to Presidential appointees obviously
hold "political jobs" and they are listed herein . Policy and Supporting Positions,
however, goes beyond that limited group. It is designed to list the jobs which
are the leading positions in the United States Government.
     The listing covers a wide variety of positions outside the competitive civil
service, including those to which appointments are made by the President,
Noncareer Executive Assignment positions in General Schedule grades 16, 17,
and 18, positions under Schedule C of the Civil Service Rules, and other ex-
cepted positions at GS- 14 (or equivalent) , and above, including selected posi-
tions under Schedules A and B of the Civil Service Rules .

    In reviewing the positions listed in this publication, the reader should be
aware that incumbents of some positions such as Noncareer Executive
Assignment and Schedule C positions-serve at the pleasure of the agency head
because the positions' excepted status reflects such considerations as advocacy
of Administration programs or policy determining responsibilities. However,
other positions, such as those in Schedule A and B, are excepted from the
competitive civil service solely because it is impractical to hold competitive
examinations for the jobs. Some agencies have a large number of employees
outside the competitive civil service-scientists and engineers in NASA, for
example-but their positions can hardly be considered political. In addition, it
should be remembered that in some of the positions listed in this publication,
the incumbent serves on a tenure basis regardless of changes in administrations.
The Comptroller General of the United States, for instance, is appointed by
the President and confirmed by the Senate. His position appears in this book,
but in fact the tenure of the incumbent will continue beyond the expiration of
the term of office of the President elected in 1976 .

     Some agencies of the Government are excluded by statute from direct
control and direction by the Administration. The Smithsonian Institution and
the Postal Service are two such agencies. The appointment of the chief officers
in these agencies is not "political"-the law prohibits the consideration of
political recommendations for appointments in the Postal Service-but the
positions are among the top policy positions in the United States Government .
So they are included.

     When preparation of this book began in August, the Civil Service Com-
mission requested that positions in agencies which have internal merit systems-
under which appointments are made only on the basis of merit and removals
are made only for cause-be excluded from this issue of Policy and Supporting
Positions even though these agencies are outside the competitive civil service
system. The Committee carefully considered the Commission's request but de-
clined to make the exclusion this year. The Committee believes that until the
Civil Service Commission has the overall capacity, including manpower and
authority, to ensure that internal agency merit systems function fairly and
effectively, the exclusion should not be made.
     NOTE. Appearing in the appendix, pp. 135-139, is a memorandum on the excepted
service positions. Also included are the Federal Salary schedules effective Oct. 1, 1976.

                                                   LEGEND
Type of appointment :
    PAS           Presidential appointment, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate.
    PA            Presidential appointment.
    PL            Positions excepted from Civil Service rules and regulations by statutes.
    NEA           Positions at GS-16, 17, and 18 authorized to be filled by Noncareer Executive Assignment
                    under Executive Order 11315 of November 17, 1966.
    A             Positions excepted from Civil Service rules and regulations, not of a confidential or policy
                    determining character for which it is not practical to hold any kind of examination.
    B
                  Positions excepted from Civil Service rules and regulations, not of a confidential or policy
                    determining character, for which it is not practical to hold a competitive examination.
    C
                  Positions of a confidential or policy determining character which are excepted from the compet-
                    itive service to which appointments may be made without examination by the Commission.
Incumbent : Applies only when bipartisan membership is required by statute.
    D             Democrat .
    I             Independent .
    R             Republican.
Tenure :
    S             Status in position.
    VP            Veteran's preference.
    VP-S          Veteran's preference with status in position.
    CA            Career Ambassador .
    CM            Career Minister.
    C             Career.
    NC            Noncareer .
    M             Military incumbent.
    FSO           Foreign Service Officer incumbent.
    FSIO          Foreign Service Information Officer incumbent.
    FSRO          Foreign Service Reserve Officer incumbent .
    FSRU          Foreign Service Reserve Unlimited Officer incumbent.
    FSS           Foreign Service Staff Officer incumbent .
Grade:
    GS            General Schedule of the Classification Act of 1949 .
    GG            Administrative grades similar to GS grades.
    WG ( WB) ,    Blue-collar positions where the pay is established at the local prevailing rate in the community.
      (WS)
    FO , FR       Foreign Service Officer Schedule .
    PE            Postal Executive Schedule .

Other:
    NE            Grade not established .
    p.d.          Per diem-daily rate of pay.
    p.h.          Per hour-hourly rate of pay.
    W.c.          Without compensation.
    I             Intermittent, when actually employed.
    NOTE : If no date is given under "Expires" column, appointment has no statutory limit.

                               APPENDIX No. 1

MEMORANDUM ON FEDERAL POSITIONS EXCEPTED FROM THE COMPETITIVE
            SYSTEM BY THE CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION

Authority
    By Executive order, the President has authorized the Civil Service Com-
mission to exempt from the competitive civil service positions which otherwise
would be subject to the Civil Service rules and regulations governing appoint-
ment and employment, generally. Civil Service Rule VI defines schedules A, B,
and C and grants authority for the Civil Service Commission to list positions
in these excepted schedules. Under Civil Service Rule IX, which established
the Executive Assignment System for positions in grades GS-16, GS-17, and
GS-18, the Commission may except positions and authorize agencies to fill
them under noncareer executive assignment.
     The Commission has been given the authority to revoke schedule A, B,
and C listings. It also periodically reviews exceptions made under Rule IX
and, after consultation with the agency concerned, revokes exceptions of execu-
tive assignment positions which no longer meet the criteria for exception.
    The Commission makes decisions about exceptions and revocations after
consideration of agency justifications and its own independent reviews and
analyses. These decisions are made by the Commissioners personally and are
not delegated.
Categories of exceptions
     Noncareer executive assignment.   These assignments are made to positions
in grades GS-16, GS-17, and GS-18 which are either of a top policy-determining
character or have a close and confidential working relationship to a top policy
official. The positions are of the type which share with Presidential appointees
the advocacy of current Administration policies and help assure control of the
executive machinery of Government by the political party in power.
      Schedule C. This schedule is for positions of a confidential or policy-
determining character not in grades GS-16 , GS-17, or GS- 18 .
    Schedule A .--This schedule is for positions, not of a confidential or policy-
determining character, for which it is not practicable to hold any kind of
examination, either competitive or noncompetitive. Examples are positions of
attorneys for which examination is forbidden by law, student interns, and
certain part-time jobs depending on residency in isolated locations .
     Schedule B. This schedule is for positions, not of a confidential or policy-
determining character, for which it is not practicable to hold a competitive
examination, but for which a noncompetitive examination (meeting basic
requirements) is required, such as student trainee positions in cooperative
education programs .
Filling excepted positions
     Agencies generally establish qualification requirements for excepted
positions, although the Civil Service Commission does this for positions listed
in schedule B and for positions authorized to be filled by noncareer executive
assignment. The Commission must approve the qualifications of all appointees
to positions in grades GS-16, GS- 17, and GS-18 .
Removals from excepted positions
    Because of their policy-determining or confidential nature, positions
authorized to be filled by noncareer executive assignment and positions in
schedule C may be subject to change in a change of National Administration.
However, some incumbents of these and other excepted positions are entitled
to certain protections, which are outlined in the table on the following page.

                                                APPENDIX NO. 3.-PAY SCHEDULES

                                            FEDERAL SALARY SCHEDULES 1976

     The information in the body of this report reflects grades or salaries as of September 3, 1976. Where an ungraded position has a
salary range, the basic entrance salary as of September 3 is shown. In some cases, these entrance salaries may have been increased
subsequent to September 3, as there was a general increase in the salaries of most Federal white-collar employees effective on the first
day of the first pay period beginning on or after October 1, 1976. This appendix shows the salaries that are in effect for the different
grades of the several pay systems after that pay increase, under Executive Order 11941, October 1, 1976.



                                                        EXECUTIVE SCHEDULE

     The Executive Schedule consists of five levels, with the following rates :
                           Level I                                                                        $66,000
                           Level II                                                                        46, 800
                           Level III                                                                       44,000
                           Level IV                                                                        41, 800
                           Level V                                                                         39, 600

    However, under Public Law 94-440, the Legislative Branch Appropriation Act, 1977, funds are not available to pay the rates
shown above to most positions at Executive Schedule levels. Instead, most positions at Executive Schedule levels are still paid only
at the rates that were in effect on September 30, 1976, as follows :
                           Level I.                                                                       $63, 000
                           Level II                                                                        44, 600
                           Level III                                                                       42,000
                           Level IV                                                                        39, 900
                           Level V                                                                         37,800

     This report does not indicate which specific positions are paid at the new rates and which positions continue to be paid at the rates
in effect on September 30, 1976.



                                                         GENERAL SCHEDULE

     Initial appointments to positions under the General Schedule are normally made at the minimum rate of the grade, although the
Civil Service Commission may authorize an agency to appoint individuals with superior qualifications at a rate above the minimum
rate, if the position is in grade GS- 11 or above.

    Step increases are granted General Schedule employees at the end of 52 weeks of service in steps 1 , 2, and 3 of each grade; at the
end of 104 weeks of service in steps 4, 5, and 6; and at the end of 156 weeks of service in steps 7, 8, and 9. An employee's work must
be determined to be of an acceptable level of competence before each step increase. In addition to the periodic step increases, an employee
whose work is outstanding may be advanced to a higher step on this basis no more often than once every 52 weeks.
     It should be noted that employees in steps 7 through 10 of GS-15, all nine steps of GS-16, all five steps of GS-17, and the single
step for GS- 18 are all paid $39,600, the rate for level V of the Executive Schedule. This salary compression results from section 5308
of title 5, United States Code, which provides that General Schedule pay may not exceed the rate for level V. (This level V ceiling also
applies to the Foreign Service schedules and the Veterans' Administration Department of Medicine and Surgery schedules, appearing
later in this appendix.)
